articles.title_orig: National security and AI figures urge DOJ to probe what Nvidia knew about chip smuggling
articles.title_zh: National security and AI figures urge DOJ to probe what Nvidia knew about chip smuggling
articles.content_orig:
A group of 15 national security experts and AI policy leaders is urging the Justice Department to investigate what Nvidia knew about the alleged smuggling of its advanced AI chips to China,  and whether the company continued doing business with customers after evidence emerged that they were illegally diverting the technology.
The letter, sent Tuesday and addressed to Attorney General Todd Blanche, asks the department to examine whether Nvidia kept selling chips to customers or middlemen after receiving evidence that they were illegally routing them to China, or whether the company “deliberately blinded itself to export control violations.”
“The United States has the world’s most advanced SI chip technology, much of it built by Nvidia,” the letter states, using the Trump administration’s “super intelligence” label for AI. “Smuggling operations threaten to undermine that lead, giving China access to hardware necessary for developing advanced SI and deploying it to boost its military capabilities and international influence.”
The 15 signatories include a range of national security experts and AI policy specialists, such as David Buckley, the Central Intelligence Agency’s former inspector general; Randy Manner, a retired Army general; Chris McGuire, a former Biden official who specialized in chips; and Brad Carson, the president of Americans for Responsible Innovation, the AI advocacy group that organized the letter.
“China and our competitors around the world have their sights set on our advanced AI chips so they can build up their AI capabilities,” Carson told NBC News. “Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are at the top of their wish lists.”
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. On Tuesday, the company’s board of directors announced that it would establish a committee dedicated to investigating national security and export control compliance.
The letter comes amid growing scrutiny of the American chipmaker and calls from Congress to investigate the extent of Nvidia’s awareness of the chips’ destination and whether the company did anything about potential smuggling.
On Tuesday, the Justice and Commerce departments shared details about their investigation of Megaspeed , the Singaporean company tied to suspected Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang. Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang is alleged to have had an affair with Megaspeed’s Huang. Megaspeed reportedly acquired billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips and is also being investigated over concerns that it — and its subsidiaries — smuggled chips to China.
In a joint statement Tuesday, the agencies said Commerce opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024, requested sales records from Nvidia in May 2025 and that Nvidia placed the company on its no-sell list the following month. Commerce investigators also conducted an in-person inspection of Megaspeed’s facilities with Singaporean law enforcement in June 2025.
The Justice Department said it took the lead in the criminal investigation after that enforcement action. The agencies said they would continue working together to pursue any criminal conduct that may have occurred.
Huang has agreed to sit for an interview with several national security-focused House committees on Dec. 1, according to House Republicans. The appearance will focus on the former CEO’s role in “a potential breach of our national security,” according to the lawmakers.
Tuesday’s letter to Blanche points to several smuggling cases the Justice Department has brought in the past year involving Nvidia. In March 2026, prosecutors charged three people in an alleged scheme in which a Southeast Asian intermediary bought roughly $2.5 billion worth of servers containing advanced AI chips. Prosecutors allege at least $510 million worth were illegally sent to China.
“Repeated attempts to route Nvidia chips to China point to a pattern that warrants a closer examination of company practices and how Nvidia responded to repeated alarming discoveries over the past several years regarding the scale of smuggling operations,” the letter states.
Smuggled chips are estimated to equal at least 25% of the chips Chinese AI companies obtained through legal routes — though the actual figure may be far larger. Many Chinese companies, including tech titans Alibaba and Tencent, have reportedly also leased chips from data centers based in Singapore, Malaysia and other southeast Asian countries.
This week, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security announced that it would close that loophole. The department said it would enact a new set of regulations limiting foreign data centers’ ability to rent their chips to Chinese companies and enacting new requirements for chip customers in five southeast Asian countries — including Singapore and Malaysia — in order to receive chips from American companies like Nvidia or AMD.
China criticized the rule. “Such actions run counter to the consensus reached between the two sides, infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, and disrupt the stability of global industrial and supply chains,” foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing in Beijing.
Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips are widely considered the most powerful available. Under current export rules, Nvidia cannot sell its top-tier chips to China, though it can sell older generation chips, from the H200 family, to China with a 25% fee taken by the White House.
The Justice Department established a new body dedicated to cracking down on AI-related crime in early November. This force, called the Super Intelligence Task Force, aims to “ensure that America’s leadership in SI is not compromised by the misuse of SI by foreign state and state-sponsored actors, transnational criminal organizations, and individual or corporate actors engaged in fraud or other unlawful conduct,” according to the Department.
Some lawmakers have clamored for stricter rules on advanced AI chip exports to China. Members of the House’s Select Committee on China have sought to restrict China’s ability to purchase chipmaking equipment and to implement stronger chip-tracking technology — to ensure that chips sent to data centers outside mainland China remain outside of the country.
Tuesday’s letter closes by urging the department “to follow the evidence wherever it leads and pursue appropriate enforcement action where violations are established.”
Jared Perlo is a technology reporter focused on AI for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_orig: EU proposes €45 billion Ukraine loan, to be repaid after Russia pays reparations
articles.title_zh: EU proposes €45 billion Ukraine loan, to be repaid after Russia pays reparations
articles.content_orig:
Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea
Europe live – latest updates
The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.
Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”
She expressed confidence all 27 member states would stand behind the loan, despite four central and eastern European countries having already ruled themselves out.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he hoped for the swift adoption of the loan and was counting on the support of all EU member states: “Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end,” he wrote on X.
Zelenskyy convinced EU leaders last month that his country faced a €70bn funding gap in 2027 . The EU pledged to cover €45bn and wants Ukraine’s other allies to cover the rest.
Only 11 months ago, the EU agreed a €90bn loan for Ukraine, which was intended to cover two-thirds of Kyiv’s military and civilian needs in 2026 and 2027. But as Russia’s attacks have escalated , the cost of Ukraine’s defence and the toll of economic disruption continue to rise.
Andrius Kubilius, the EU defence commissioner, said Ukraine’s military spending was increasingly dominated by drones. Ukraine, he told reporters, expected Russia to use 10m drones this year and 20m in 2027. “Ukraine with EU assistance needs to match – and will match,” he said.
The EU loan is split into two parts: €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian needs, including funding essential services, such as schools and hospitals.
Von der Leyen expressed confidence that all member states would support the loan because “all 27 member states say very clearly that they want to support Ukraine”. She said member states could choose to support Ukraine’s civilian needs, rather than military spending.
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, however, have said they do not intend to take part in the latest funding round for Ukraine, prompting a warning from the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, that he would block the EU’s seven-year budget unless all countries got onboard.
The four central and eastern countries are net beneficiaries of the EU budget, while Germany is the largest payer and Ukraine’s biggest EU donor.
The EU wants Ukraine’s non-EU allies – such as Norway, the UK and Canada – to find €25bn for Kyiv in 2027.
after newsletter promotion
The EU proposal included provisions “to help other countries to help us”, a senior commission official said. Brussels has proposed that G7 countries that provide new loans get guarantees that the borrowing can be repaid with future profits from Russia’s frozen assets.
The profits from the Russian assets are being used to repay a €45bn loan issued by the G7 to Ukraine in 2024.
Countries with a triple-A credit rating could opt to provide guarantees to the EU budget up to €5bn to expand European borrowing for Ukraine on capital markets. The commission has identified six countries that fall into this category: Australia, Canada, Liechtenstein, Norway, Singapore and Switzerland.
EU officials previously said the UK and other allies needed to do more to support Ukraine in 2027, arguing that the EU was shouldering too much of the burden. The UK subsequently pledged a £10bn economic and military support package for Ukraine.
Zelenskyy said: “The UK, Canada, Japan, and Norway have been helping tremendously in our defence of life, and establishing clear rules under which they can provide further aid in conjunction with the EU will help even more.”

articles.title_orig: Trump in China for nuclear talks with Xi Jinping, Putin
articles.title_zh: Trump in China for nuclear talks with Xi Jinping, Putin
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday morning ahead of historic trilateral talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.
Xi earlier welcomed President Donald Trump on the tarmac, which he said was a sign of reciprocity after Trump personally greeted him at the airport during a visit to the U.S. in September.
Trump is attending a welcome banquet alongside Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
Trump is in China for the APEC summit, which President Xi opened with calls for free trade and greater cooperation around artificial intelligence. Highly anticipated talks with Xi and Putin are set for Thursday.
Xi said Thursday's leaders' meeting would discuss "measures to expand mutual openness, explore paths for innovation-driven growth, and broaden practical cooperation in various fields," according to Chinese state media. The Chinese president told Trump he wanted to "advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship between China and the US based on respect, fairness and reciprocity," according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua. Trump said he was confident the visit would advance bilateral relations and prove successful, Xinhua reported.
Xi said: "We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition."
Putin has also addressed the summit , saying sanctions imposed on Russia have backfired and strengthened his nation.
The much-anticipated meeting between the three world leaders is set to take place on Thursday, with discussions expected to center on the Iran war and Russia's war in Ukraine.
Though expectations for any concrete outcome are low, Trump, Xi and Putin are expected to hold in-depth discussions on issues crucial for world peace and strategic stability, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry said Monday.
North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un could attend the summit, which is a forum of 21 APEC member economies.
Trump flew in from Manila, Philippines, where he started a three-day visit to Asia and met key regional allies including Japan, India and Australia.
The APEC host city Shenzhen has been dubbed one of China's "Silicon Valleys" and has been a major hub for China's internet and artificial intelligence companies.
Beijing will position itself against what it calls "unilateralism and protectionism," with trade, artificial intelligence, and the Middle East expected to dominate the meeting's agenda.
Xi held several bilateral meetings with leaders on the sidelines Wednesday, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, with whom he discussed trade and commerce. Seoul's readout of the meeting also said the pair discussed peace on the Korean Peninsula, but this was omitted from Beijing's record of the talks.
The Chinese leader also met Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Vietnamese President To Lam earlier in the week.
Xi met with Putin earlier Wednesday, before Trump's arrival. The Chinese president called for greater cooperation between the two countries and spoke of providing a more stable and predictable business environment, according to Chinese state media, while promoting a "multipolar world and democratization of international relations."
Putin said Russia was looking to expand cooperation in trade, energy and education. The reports did not address Russia's war in Ukraine or the Iran war.
Trump will also hold bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, amid hopes the pair can secure a lasting trade truce beyond January 2027. The meeting comes as the U.S. seeks to curb exports of artificial intelligence chips and amid concerns that Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China.

articles.title_orig: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is a cultural and economic earthquake. Brace yourself.
articles.title_zh: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is a cultural and economic earthquake. Brace yourself.
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, against the backdrop of the Miami-inspired Vice City. Rockstar Games hide caption
I want to tell you about the time I saw Bigfoot. I want to tell you about sitting in the rain on a city street in a muscle car and prepping to rob a bank while lightning split the sky between high-rise condo towers in the distance and the drum fill from In The Air Tonight played on the radio. I want to tell you about gunfights and fistfights, the perfect satire of radio commercials and how the sunrise looks over Ocean Beach. But more than any of that, I want to tell you about the time an alligator bit my mom.
It happened in the backyard of an abandoned house with a rotting inground pool. My mom, Mia Caminos (mother of Lucia Caminos, one of the two leads in Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI , probably the most highly anticipated video game sequel of all time), was thrilled by the pool. Standing there, amid the artfully rendered weeds and trash, she spread her arms and told me to use my imagination, to see her vision for this ruin of a house with its upmarket water feature, in a scabby neighborhood on the outskirts of Vice City. She speaks in tones of increasingly frantic desperation because she has already put money down on this house, sight unseen. All of her money, actually, in hopes of flipping it and selling it fast to keep her startup real estate business afloat.
Lucia begins her epic as a petty criminal. Rockstar Games hide caption
The pool is still half full of water. There's a dirty, sodden mattress floating in it. And as if this is the main thing standing between her and success, Mia is fixated on getting it out of the pool.
Help me, Lucia , she says.
And, dutifully, I do. Playing as Lucia, I grab hold, mash buttons, help my mom drag away the wet, heavy, stinking mattress. And just as we get it up and over the lip of the pool that's going to be the thing that makes this wreck of a house suddenly desirable – that's when the alligator lunges out of the murky water, grabs my mom by the arm and tries to drag her back in.
This is a story about folly, fixation, unrealistic expectations of success at the ass-end of late capitalism, and the vicious, whip-crack cruelty of predators who lie in wait for anyone trying to improve a terrible situation.
But then I shoot the alligator in the head before it can eat my mom. Because this is also a story about violence, and how sometimes (maybe all the times), the loud, cathartic rip of gunfire is the only solution left for people who have already lost so much and can't bear to see one more thing taken from them.
It's a story about my mom and an alligator, sure.
It is also the story of GTA6
Grand Theft Auto VI returns to Vice City and its Florida-inspired environs. Rockstar Games hide caption
But let's back up a little. For anyone who has somehow missed the shrieking, neon-and-swamp-water marketing onslaught over the past several days, weeks, months and years, Grand Theft Auto VI is the newest release from Rockstar Games. It is a Bonnie and Clyde love story, a knife-edged satire of modern American culture and politics, an unapologetic murder simulator, a love letter to 50 years of crime movies, and a thoughtful, emotional meditation on the sacrifices, small and large, that we make for family. A massive open world game set in the fictional state of Leonida (based on the very real state of Florida), it represents a return to a location that Rockstar hasn't visited in-depth since its 2002 release of GTA: Vice City , and is the first new game in the franchise since GTA5 launched in 2013. According to estimates, it already earned over $1.5 billion in pre-sales and will likely make a total of $3 to $5 billion in its first week , which could make it the largest single entertainment product launch ever.
Fans have been waiting years for it. They have created libraries worth of lore and theories and dissected trailers frame-by-frame. To discount the overheated environment into which this singular work of art is being released would be doing a disservice both to it and the legions of salivating prognosticators who have made guessing the number of bird species included in-game , or speculating on the square mileage of its map, their entire personalities.
While Vice City remains the game's hub, most of its map is actually rural or wild. Rockstar Games hide caption
Now, though, they know it all. We all do. We know that GTA6 is expansive, covering everything from the Keys (where the game starts) to the hilly, forested north, with Vice City in all its grimy, pastel-colored splendor at the beating heart of it. It is a playground, equal parts gorgeous and maniacal, and in all that space the developers have given us a thousand different things to do. You can rob a bank or take a bike ride, go fishing, hunt trophy animals, visit strip clubs, rob random civilians, street race, fly drones, eat a sandwich, work out, manage your family savings account, jump a sports car off the top of a building, steal a plane, punch out a convenience store clerk, fight a bear or, yes, just wander out toward the horizon and study the birds. And while some of that is fun and all of it is diverting (at least for a little while), none of it is the ostensible point. The game-y part of the game — the hundred extras and time-wasters that players have come to expect from open-world projects in general, and GTA specifically — is not what makes it matter.
What matters is Mia and the alligator, Lucia and the gun. It's the multi-pronged, exquisitely balanced narrative about poverty and rigged systems that makes it hard to turn away from GTA while you're playing and impossible not to think about when you're away.
Jason and his pal, Cal, shoot pool. Rockstar Games hide caption
Lucia is an ex-con, a car thief and a small-time criminal who got caught trying to rob a payday loan joint and starts the game in jail. Her partner, Jason Duval, is a veteran, dishonorably discharged, now making a living flying loads for a local coke dealer down in the Keys and living rent-free in one of his properties. Jason skims a little on the coke deals, wears flip-flops and drinks beer in the sun, and goes fishing with his best friend Cal (played with genius-level goofy, drunken paranoia and dopey bravado by Bobby Moynihan). Jason and Lucia have a kid, Tomás, who is currently living with Lucia's family, and every plan they have is about getting right by the law, making a few bucks and grabbing a chance at finally being a family.
Only there are complications — surprisingly banal ones at first (like not being able to open a checking account because of their bad credit) — that slowly ramp up into huge ones across 60-odd hours of main story gameplay that see Jason and Lucia (both of whom are playable characters) graduate from knocking over liquor stores in a beat-up El Camino, to pulling off elaborate heists in the middle of Vice City which will have you dangling from a net suspended from a cargo helicopter hauling 200 tons of cocaine. It goes from Badlands to Die Hard with the speed of a muscle car, all bright chrome and barking straight pipes. From True Romance to Heat like that's just the natural arc of any American love story.
And what's remarkable about the whole bloody delight is that it remains, until its final operatic moments, so surprisingly grounded. This is a somewhat more mature GTA than its predecessors, trading aliens, cannibal cultists and whacked-out drug trips for wellness influencers, local politics and the music industry. Jason and Lucia's relationship is the superstructure around which the entire narrative is built, and it's a dynamic thing that must be maintained in a dozen little ways — making coffee in the morning, opening doors for each other, date nights (even if that means robbing a jewelry store together), or holding hands as you walk toward yet another betrayal by someone you thought you could trust. articles.title_orig: The Latest: Trump arrives in China, seeking to reinforce US's status as world’s leading tech power
articles.title_zh: The Latest: Trump arrives in China, seeking to reinforce US's status as world’s leading tech power
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
President Donald Trumparrived in the Philippines on Tuesday, where he was scheduled to meet regional partners, talk trade, and seek a break from a series of setbacks at home, ranging from a major disruption to the U.S. aviation industry to a scandal that has shaken the global AI industry.
Manila , the Philippine capital, is Trump’s first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin , and, according to Trump, potentially for a meeting with North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un .
Trump administration details its $50 billion request for aviation system improvements
The Trump administration has formally updated its request to lawmakers for $50.1 billion to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system and to make other improvements at airports.
A letter to key lawmakers dated Tuesday says that less than 24 hours after the administration’s request of $30.1 billion, “the urgent need for this investment became undeniable.” That’s when outdated equipment disrupted aircraft communications and radar feeds, forcing the Federal Aviation Administration to initiate a nationwide ground stop.
The request to lawmakers calls for $10.1 billion for updating the nation’s air traffic control system. Another $10 billion would go to boosting airport infrastructure.
Meanwhile, $10 billion would go to replace or refurbish terminals at high-impact hubs. Another $10 billion would go to construct five new traffic control centers and $10 billion would go to improving or replacing up to 140 FAA-owned air traffic control towers.
Trump’s pick to lead the Navy focuses on shipbuilding in his opening statements
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators at his confirmation hearing Tuesday that he’ll focus on revitalizing shipbuilding in an effort to expand the nation’s fleet of warships.
But Cao avoided potentially thorny topics that are likely to come up before the Senate Armed Services Committee. Those include the Iran war, the recent firings of Navy admirals and the waiver Cao will need from Congress to become Navy secretary because he left active duty less than seven years ago.
Cao also spoke of his biography, which includes fleeing Vietnam with his family right before the fall of Saigon in the 1970s. He also focused on his 25 years of service in the Navy.
“I spent my entire adult life serving in the United States Navy special operations community with multiple combat deployments to Iraq, Afghanistan and Somalia,” Cao said.
Bipartisan concerns arise over forces being ‘stretched thin’ during Navy secretary hearing
Despite deep divisions over the Iran war, the Republican and Democratic leaders of the Senate Armed Services Committee voiced a unified concern over the impact the ongoing military operation and internal issues at the Department of Defense have had on the U.S. Navy.
“Our sailors and Marines are our greatest asset, but they cannot sustain an increasingly demanding operational tempo without adequate support,” GOP Sen. Roger Wicker, the committee chair, said during his opening statement.
His Democratic counterpart, Sen. Jack Reed, echoed his worry, saying that “disruption” from high-ranking officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, “sends the wrong signal to our sailors and Marines.”
Confirmation hearing for Trump’s nominee to lead the US Navy gets underway
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump loyalist and combat veteran, appeared Tuesday before the Senate Armed Services Committee as he seeks the permanent top civilian job during a particularly volatile time in Washington. It’s the first step in a nomination process that could turn into a fierce debate over the Iran war, military transparency and the well-being of American sailors.
Cao also faces the extra hurdle of needing a waiver from Congress, because he left active-duty service less than seven years ago.
ASEAN-US dinner menu features American surf and turf
The main course was a pairing of U.S. beef tenderloin and lobster tail, served with a truffle potato puree, glazed baby carrots, oyster mushrooms and a wine sauce, according to details shared by the White House.
Courses before the main included ratatouille, goose liver mousse and burrata cheese salad with heirloom tomatoes, walnuts, balsamic glaze and olive oil.
Chocolate-covered cake with roasted almonds and salted caramel ice cream was served for dessert.
Trump’s pick for Navy secretary likely to face Iran war questions during confirmation hearing
He’s scheduled to testify before a Senate committee Tuesday, the first step in a nomination process that could turn into a fierce debate over the Iran war, military transparency and the well-being of American sailors.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump loyalist and combat veteran, is seeking the permanent top civilian job during a particularly volatile time in Washington. He also faces the extra hurdle of needing a waiver from Congress, because he left active-duty service less than seven years ago.
Cao will face the current Congress, with Republicans still in charge. But he’s likely to face intense scrutiny from Democrats over aspects of the Iran war, including major damage to the service’s 5th Fleet headquarters in Bahrain, as well as the recent firings of Navy officials.
Trump could meet Imelda Marcos during summit in Philippines
Officials are arranging a possible brief reunion between Trump and an old acquaintance — Imelda Marcos — if she’s well enough and gets her doctors’ nod.
Now 97 and using a wheelchair, the former jet-set Philippine first lady and mother of the incumbent president partied in New York decades ago in her heyday as the controversial wife of a strongman leader, who was to be ousted in a pro-democracy 1986 “People Power” public uprising.
But the friendship with Trump endured, with Trump often asking President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and other Philippine officials: “How’s Imelda?” Philippine Ambassador to Washington Jose Manuel Romualdez told The Associated Press.
“Personal connections are very important to him,” Romualdez said.
When the Philippine leader met Trump in the White House last year, he carried a note from his mother that thanked the U.S. president for his strong backing of the Philippines. “President Trump was very happy and told Marcos, ‘Please say hello to your mother,’” according to Romualdez.
US and Thailand sign joint statement affirming terms of forthcoming trade deal
At a brief signing ceremony in Manila, Trump said Thailand has agreed to eliminate all tariffs on U.S. exports and remove “substantial” nontariff barriers on American automobiles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol and poultry.
Trump said Thailand will also be buying an estimated $2.6 billion in additional U.S. agricultural products and “that makes our farmers very happy.”
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said there’s still “a little more to do” before the agreement itself is finalized and that it should be “ready for us to sign real soon.”
Trump still talking about possible meetings with Russia, North Korea leaders
Trump says North Korea’s leader would like to meet with him in China later this week. And he’s open to sitting down with Russian President Vladimir Putin, too.
But so far, it appears neither meeting has been arranged.
Trump landed in the Philippines on Tuesday for talks with Asia-Pacific leaders. On Thursday, he’s due in Shenzhen, China, for more talks, including a historic three-way confab with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
“We’ll see what happens,” Trump said in Manila when reporters asked about North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

articles.title_orig: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.title_zh: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.content_orig:
Hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators.
Even as it announced the new products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.
The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.
Hims in late October launched an early access list for the upcoming peptide offerings, and more than 10,000 people signed up within 15 days, a company spokesperson said in a statement.
None of the company's specific compounded products are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. But Hims said they are authorized by law and formulated by pharmacies "that adhere to rigorous quality standards and are licensed and inspected by state boards of pharmacy."
The products include compounded formulations of sermorelin, a peptide that stimulates growth-hormone release and is marketed for recovery, body composition and anti-aging; glutathione, a peptide promoted ‌for anti-aging and athletic recovery; and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, or NAD+, a coenzyme that plays a role in cellular metabolism.
The company will also offer compounded versions of vitamin B-12, a vitamin needed to make red blood cells, build DNA, and maintain healthy nerve function, and L-carnitine, an amino acid derivative that helps the body turn fat into energy. The FDA has approved certain prescription forms of both peptides for established medical uses, primarily for diagnosed deficiencies in those compounds.
Hims said it plans to add more peptides and therapies made in the U.S. over time. That includes BPC-157, an unapproved peptide derived from a protein found in human gastric juice that is marketed for healing processes. The company also aims to introduce another unapproved peptide called TB-500, which is derived from a naturally occurring protein in the body and is marketed for broader, systemic soft-tissue recovery and flexibility. Most of the research on both has been conducted in animals, not humans.
To receive the products, members on the Hims platform will start with an assessment of health history and goals with a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies, who can tailor a personalized plan to their needs, if appropriate.
The company said it intends to use its communication platform to check in with patients and ensure they are seeing desired results.
"If they're not, we need to do something about it," Dr. Anant Vinjamoori, Hims chief medical officer, told CNBC. "We need to, you know, adjust the dose when that's appropriate, or in some cases consider other compounds that's maybe a better fit. And of course, there will also be cases when we need to refer people to other care options."
However, Vinjamoori said there's still uncertainty over how to best use the peptides.
"We don't have all of this data that we're used to having with compounds like this," he said. "We have the opportunity to get it right, and I think we see that as our responsibility with a company of our size, our skill, and resources to really lead."
Vinjamoori added that people who have serious illnesses, such as cardiovascular disease, liver disease and kidney disease, will not be candidates for the compounds for now.
Meanwhile, Andrew Huberman, a well known neuroscientist, podcaster and Stanford University School of Medicine professor who recently joined Hims' board of directors, in a statement called compounds "real medical treatments, not just a wellness trend." He said Hims provides safe access through "trusted sourcing and physician oversight."
But health experts raised concerns about the broader mainstream marketing of peptides in the U.S. and accessing them on telehealth platforms.
"With peptides, I think you have to view them the same way you would view any drug that hasn't been rigorously tested," said Joshua Kritzer, a chemistry professor at Tufts University. "Without actual testing, all you have is anecdotal information, and that's just not enough information to put a substance in your body."
Kritzer said the lack of large clinical trials means researchers can't rule out potentially serious, rare complications from peptides — the kinds of risks that have led regulators to reject or pull otherwise effective drugs from the market after they underwent comprehensive testing in humans.
Without that testing, it's also unclear how telehealth firms, physicians and pharmacies can make decisions about what doses patients should take, said Paul Knoepfler, a cell biology and human anatomy professor at UC Davis Health. While some people rely on anecdotal data from real peptide users, "the dosing for these products really has not been established," he added.
Knoepfler said one risk is that injecting too much of a synthetic peptide into patients could trigger "weird immune responses that are really bad for one's health" because the body might recognize it as foreign.
"With the peptides, it's very loosey-goosey," Knoepfler told CNBC. "How does one even know what would be the effective amount for whatever you're hoping it will do, and what amount would have more risks?"
But he said the more contact patients can have with physicians around taking a compounded peptide, the better. Providers, including those tied to telehealth firms, should make sure patients are well-informed about the possible risks and unknowns of a given product and consider their preexisting conditions, cancer history and other medications, Knoepfler said.
That appears to be consistent with the approach Hims & Hers is taking. The company says patients who use the peptide and longevity products can also use its Care+ offering, which pairs treatment with ongoing support. That includes twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress and the ability to message providers trained in peptide therapy around the clock with any questions.
Still, Kritzer argued that having a doctor who only knows a patient from online, essentially mail-order platforms or websites "is not enough supervision to put you on a prescription medication," especially an unapproved one.
Hims' ability to legally sell some of these peptides stems from a major shift in federal oversight by the Health and Human Services Department. It issued a policy in October that says the Food and Drug Administration will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or physicians that compound and dispense six unapproved peptides while formal rules are reviewed.
In practice, that means these pharmacies and other firms can now offer them, even though the peptides aren't yet on the FDA's official list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make. It does not translate to formal approval of the specific peptides.
The policy followed a 2023 decision by the Biden administration where the FDA restricted compounding pharmacies from producing popular peptide formulations due to safety, impurity and immune-reaction concerns.
HHS Secretary ​Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides, calling himself a "big fan" of the treatments and arguing that restrictions were driving Americans to potentially unsafe products from overseas. Kennedy has previously described using BPC-157 to treat a muscle injury.
The announcement also comes after Hims in February 2025 acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility equipped with advanced peptide synthesizers.
The evidence for peptide efficacy varies by compound.

articles.title_orig: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.title_zh: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.content_orig:
On November 17, 2026, the security research company Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) , a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the most widely used Java runtime. Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, it scores 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The flaw affects Java. OpenJDK published a security advisory and Oracle released patched builds in its November 2026 Critical Patch Update the same day, at 21:00 UTC.
The vulnerability lets a remote attacker with no credentials send malformed Base64 data to a Java application and overwrite memory next to the decoded output. Calif turned that overwrite into a leak of heap memory, similar to Heartbleed , and into remote code execution. Calif demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution against Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate in their default configurations, and post-authentication remote code execution against Apache Kafka, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker.
Cloudflare has released a new set of rules in the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset designed to detect malformed Base64 input patterns associated with this vulnerability. The rules are available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans and are enabled by default with the Log action because malformed input and some benign application-specific token formats can resemble exploitation attempts. Blocking by default could therefore disrupt legitimate traffic. Customers can review matching requests in Security Events now and change the rules action to Block once they confirm it does not affect legitimate traffic.Â
The WAF is an additional layer of defense, not a replacement for the patch. Java4Shell can be reached through paths a WAF does not see, like outbound TLS responses, and the only complete fix is to update the Java runtime. Our analysts continue to monitor attack activity and will update the rules as new techniques and variations appear. You can track rule changes in the WAF changelog and get more information on how the vulnerability develops on the dedicated Cloudflare Zero Wire briefing .
We have seen no indication so far that Java4Shell was exploited on Cloudflare infrastructure.
Base64 is a common way to represent binary data as text. Java applications decode Base64 when they process authentication headers, tokens, file uploads and many network messages. To decode it faster, OpenJDK replaces frequently used code with specialized machine code, called intrinsics. On supported x86-64 processors, the Base64 intrinsic uses AVX-512 instructions to process 64 bytes at a time.
The bug sits in the handwritten assembly that handles the final characters of the input. When the tail of the input contains padding characters (=) in a position where valid Base64 never places them, the routine calculates a negative output length. That invalid length turns into a full 64-byte write. For a 65-character input, made of 64 characters followed by a single =, OpenJDK allocates a 50-byte output array and then writes 62 bytes past its end.
Java eventually rejects the input as invalid and throws an exception. By then, the neighboring memory has already been overwritten. An application's own input validation does not help, because the corruption happens inside the decoder before the application can reject the data.
The simplest trigger is 64 A characters followed by =. On OpenJDK 17, the trigger needs 128 characters followed by =, because the threshold for the fast code path is higher.
Exploitation is not point-and-shoot. The overwritten bytes are mostly fixed values, and the attacker controls only where the write lands. To build a working exploit, Calif arranged the Java heap so that the overflow enlarged neighboring arrays, which gave them first a way to read heap memory and then a way to write chosen bytes. Each target application requires its own exploit chain. Calif reported developing its first working local exploit in about three hours with the help of AI agents, so we expect other attackers to build exploit chains quickly.
Java4Shell affects a system only when all the following conditions are true:
OpenJDK 17.0.6 or newer, including distributions built from OpenJDK: Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica, SAP SapMachine, Red Hat OpenJDK, Oracle OpenJDK, Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM for JDK. Check Oracle's advisory for the exact list of affected Oracle builds.
x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI support, such as Intel Xeon Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids, or AMD EPYC and Ryzen Zen 4 or newer. ARM64 processors are not affected.
The application decodes attacker-controlled Base64 data with the standard Java decoder.
Many applications bundle their own Java runtime, and container images ship with a fixed Java Development Kit (JDK). Upgrading the system Java package does not update those copies, and it does not replace a Java virtual machine (JVM) that is already running. Every updated service needs a restart.
If you cannot update immediately, Calif documents two JVM startup flags that remove the vulnerable code path:
Both flags require a restart and may reduce performance for workloads that decode large amounts of Base64. They buy time while you patch. They do not replace the update.
Patching every Java runtime takes time, especially when JDKs are bundled inside applications and container images. Cloudflare WAF can reduce your exposure while you patch. A new managed rule, available on paid plans and enabled in Log mode by default, detects the malformed Base64 input that triggers Java4Shell. For Business and Enterprise customers, WAF attack score adds a machine learning layer that scores each request for remote code execution payloads, which helps catch variations and bypass attempts that signature-based rules can miss.
Protection for paid plans has been released as part of the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset (Ruleset ID efb7b8c949ac4650a09736fc376e9aee). The rule is enabled by default with the Log action, because blocking by default could cause false positives on legitimate Base64 traffic. To review its matches, go to Security > Security Analytics > Events and filter by the rule ID. If the matches are not legitimate traffic, change the rule action to Block: go to Security > Settings, edit the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, search for CVE-2026-114938 and set the rule action to Block. Alternatively, you can follow the link to review your configuration on the Zero Wire briefing.

articles.title_orig: Trump and Marcos Share a Moment Over Jollibee Fried Chicken
articles.title_zh: Trump and Marcos Share a Moment Over Jollibee Fried Chicken
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump missed out on a chance to stand up for Kentucky's finest in a fast-food contest with a fellow world leader.
Trump, 80, attended a bilateral state luncheon hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., 69, at Malacañang Palace in Manila on Wednesday.
The sit-down was designed to tout a new bilateral trade deal and praise the U.S.–Philippines alliance, but the Filipino leader couldn't resist a swipe at the fast food-obsessed president… and his beloved Kentucky Fried Chicken.
"Bongbong," as he is known, revealed that he ordered Jollibee chicken for Trump and his team on Tuesday evening.
"Since you're strapped for time, I thought the taste of Manila might be good. So last night, I asked my staff to have some Jollibee delivered as a late-night snack for you and your delegation," he said.
He continued: "Jollibee is a very popular chain. And one of their main products is fried chicken. And we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity."
Jollibee is a national treasure in the Philippines, and Ferdinand Marcos Jr., who has been president since 2022, is clearly proud of it.
"Oh, wow," Trump muttered. "Fantastic." He failed to stand up for America's most popular chicken joint, and gave Bongbong the win.
The Filipino leader concluded: "So we thought that will give you a taste of Manila. And I think maybe I hope some of your staff was also able to partake."
While KFC still dwarfs Jollibee in U.S. store count, 3,700 to 107, Marcos appeared to be nodding to American reader polls. For three consecutive years (2024–2026), Jollibee's signature "Chickenjoy", which costs between $6 and $9 for a single piece, has been voted the No. 1 fast-food fried chicken in the U.S. in USA Today's 10 Best Readers' Choice Awards—beating out American staples including KFC, Chick-fil-A, Popeyes, and Raising Cane's.
Trump appeared intrigued, perhaps as a businessman, but also as a fast food lover.
In 2017, Trump's former campaign manager Corey Lewandowski wrote in Let Trump Be Trump : "On Trump Force One, there were four major food groups: McDonald's, Kentucky Fried Chicken, pizza, and Diet Coke."
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the anti-vax crusader leading the MAHA movement , even told The Katie Miller Podcast that "I don't know how he's alive," given that the president constantly eats "really bad food," including McDonald's and candy.

articles.title_orig: The Fed's AI Bank Run Nightmare Is Suddenly Coming True
articles.title_zh: The Fed's AI Bank Run Nightmare Is Suddenly Coming True
articles.content_orig:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday called for aggressive action against inflation , saying the central bank needs to "shock people" as prices continue to rise more than he expected.
In the near term, the policymaker told CNBC in a live interview that a half percentage point increase in the Fed's benchmark rate is probably necessary at the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
He said the central bank needs to reverse the three quarter-point reductions from last year and may need to do more.
"I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman during a " Squawk Box " interview. "If you really want to get it down, you've got to start taking more aggressive actions."
"You might need to, like, shock people," he said.
Futures prices are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the FOMC's December meeting. They also are anticipating another move in January, followed by at least one additional increase before the end of 2027, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge.
Waller said the Fed wouldn't necessarily have to approve a half-point hike in December if it raised rates by a quarter point and signaled another move coming in January. However, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has been against that kind of forward guidance on grounds that it ties policymakers' hands.
"If you're not going to signal this very clearly to markets, you're going in January, my view is then you have to go 50 [basis points] in December to put it in place and get it done," he said.
Recent statements from other central bankers indicate a range of opinions , though most agree that more policy tightening is needed to bring down inflation.
In a speech Tuesday, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested as many as four hikes by the spring of 2027. Some Fed officials, including regional Presidents Beth Hammack of Cleveland and Lorie Logan of Dallas, have endorsed more gradual tightening.
However, continued inflation above the Fed's 2% target might push officials into a more aggressive stance.
The FOMC approved its first interest rate hike in more than three years in September, and then held rates steady at its October meeting. While inflation has continued to run hot since then, other Fed officials seem less eager to drop the policy hammer as heavily as Waller.
"I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action," New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday in a conversation with Axios. "I think what we've been doing over the last past few months is ... working well. We're collecting the data, analyzing it, having the debate and making a decision."
The Fed in 2025 approved three rate cuts amid worries over the labor market and the belief that inflation would continue to moderate toward the central bank's 2% goal.
However, inflation reignited earlier this year after the strikes the U.S. and Israel launched against Iran in late February. Energy prices spiked while tariff impacts lingered, keeping most inflation readings above 3% .
"First of all, you've got to take back the three insurance cuts we put in last year," Waller said. "If the policy rate last summer in 2025 wasn't bringing inflation down, getting back to that isn't going to bring it down. So we may have to go above ... three hikes plus maybe some more to get it to start actually coming back down."
The FOMC later Wednesday will release minutes from the October meeting.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.content_orig:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, panel Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify, Scott said. The agreements to appear voluntarily come as pressure builds on Capitol Hill to investigate Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which led to his ouster at the chipmaker he founded.
"They both have agreed," Scott said. "We will hopefully have this done before Christmas."
Huang reached an agreement on Tuesday with the chairmen of three House committees for a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1 jointly before the three panels. Scott had asked Huang to appear publicly in the Senate.
Scott said the appearances will provide the committee with "more information about what they knew, when they knew it and why they didn't do something about it."
The outgoing banking committee chair also homed in on Lutnick, calling for answers as to why the commerce secretary did not act after being warned about Megaspeed — the Singaporean company where the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive. Nvidia sold its chips to Megaspeed, which U.S. investigators suspect of diverting them to China.
"They were warned as early as March of this year, several months ago, that Megaspeed should be on the 'entity list,'" Scott said, referring to a Commerce Department list of companies the U.S. views as national security risks. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security "didn't do it, Howard didn't do it, we want to know why."
Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have been embroiled in an intra-administration battle as the fallout from the Huang affair grows. Bessent on CNBC on Friday appeared to blame Lutnick for a lack of action on Megaspeed.
"You will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said, referring to Commerce and noting his department has long supported imposing restrictions on Megaspeed.
A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment on Scott's announcement that he has agreed to appear.
Huang's upcoming appearances are likely just the start of the embattled former CEO's problems on Capitol Hill. Democrats will take control of Congress in January and have demanded sweeping investigations into the affair and Huang's cozy relationship with President Donald Trump .

articles.title_orig: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.title_zh: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.content_orig:
Medicare Part B premiums will rise by 3.2% in 2027, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services announced Tuesday .
The standard premium will rise by $6.50 per month to $209.40, totaling a $78-per-year increase.
The 2027 increase, far smaller than the nearly 10% increase enrollees faced in 2026, is in line with the 3.25% increase projected by Medicare's trustees.
According to the CMS, "The increase in the 2027 Part B standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending."
Here's what you need to know before the increases are applied in January.
The Medicare Part A deductible, which beneficiaries pay if they are admitted to the hospital, will rise by $40 to $1,776 in 2027.
The Medicare Part A premium will be $597 per month, a $32 increase from $565 in 2026.
According to the CMS , it is paid by:
Anyone aged 65 and older with fewer than 40 quarters of coverage, plus certain people with disabilities.
Uninsured people aged 65 and older with fewer than 30 quarters, and certain people with disabilities who have exhausted other entitlements.
Those with at least 30 quarters (or a spouse with 30 or more quarters) will pay a reduced rate of $328.
Roughly 9% of people with Part B pay an income-related surcharge on top of their monthly premium.
The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries will increase by $9 to $292 in 2027.
In 2027, individuals with modified adjusted gross income above $112,000, or couples filing jointly above $224,000, will pay more. At the top tier, individuals with an income of $500,000 or more and couples earning $750,000 or more will pay $711.80 a month.
Married people who live with their spouse but file separate tax returns pay the standard $209.40 Part B premium if their income is $112,000 or less. Above that, they pay a total of $670 a month, rising to $711.80 for those earning $388,000 or more.
A small group of kidney transplant patients can keep Part B coverage of immunosuppressive drugs for a standard premium of $125.70 a month.
Those with higher incomes who pay Part D premiums face separate income-related surcharges between $15.40 and $96.40 a month on top of their plan's premium. The surcharge is paid to Medicare and is either deducted from Social Security checks or paid directly.
People who have their Part B premium deducted from their Social Security checks will keep less of the cost-of-living adjustment next year.
For the average retiree, the $6.50 Part B increase will eat into the $75 monthly COLA boost, leaving them with about $68.50 more a month.
Most beneficiaries will have the standard $209.40 Part B premium withheld from their checks. Higher earners will pay more, with total monthly Part B premiums reaching as much as $711.80 and Part D surcharges up to $96.40.

articles.title_orig: Wall Street prepares for Anthropic IPO frenzy, despite broader AI stock slump
articles.title_zh: Wall Street prepares for Anthropic IPO frenzy, despite broader AI stock slump
articles.content_orig:
Retail investor Dan Shetty is so eager to get in on the Anthropic initial public offering that he "drained" his Roth IRA and moved roughly $12,000 from Fidelity to Robinhood for a chance to participate.
"I don't want to tell my grandkids that I didn't invest in Anthropic and I didn't invest in OpenAI during the AI bubble," he said.
Shetty's enthusiasm is shared by many, with excitement among small investors for the blockbuster IPO expected to be off the charts. Vanda Research estimates that Anthropic could see approximately $250 million of retail net buying when it starts trading Thursday, double the size of SpaceX's IPO.
"That would be far and away the largest amount of net retail buying of any stock that we've seen in our data on the first day of its listing," Jai Malhi, senior strategist at Vanda, said in an interview with CNBC.
The artificial intelligence laboratory — which will trade on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol ANT — is selling 825 million shares at an expected price range of $70 to $78 per share in the IPO, though sources told CNBC the stock is likely to price above that range . Individual investors are expected to be allocated as much as 20% in that initial offering. And if Vanda's figures prove correct, the buying enthusiasm will be big as regular trading begins.
Founded less than six years ago, Anthropic aims to raise as much as $64.4 billion, giving it a valuation of $1.405 trillion. If demand is especially strong, Anthropic could even raise more than the record $85.7 billion that SpaceX sold in its record IPO in June.
The tech trade has been in turmoil since Jensen Huang's departure last week as Nvidia CEO raised questions about the future of AI financing. Before then, a potential slowdown in data center development resulting from Democratic victories in the 2026 midterm elections, and signs of moderation in the capital expenditures boom, had already spooked investors.
These all stand in marked contrast to the market backdrop in place at the time of the SpaceX IPO. In June, both positioning and sentiment were high, Malhi said. The Anthropic IPO could see a different dynamic, however. Demand could be strong across the entire investor spectrum given that sentiment is depressed, meaning that the bar to beat expectations is "much easier to overcome," he explained.
"What we're seeing across both retail and institutional positioning is that there is plenty of dry powder to take part in this IPO," the strategist said.
For the 27-year-old New Yorker Shetty, who himself works at agentic data platform Data Workers, this is his first time vying to take part in an IPO. He said Anthropic's emphasis on "safety first" drew his interest.
"I've been telling all of my friends, 'If you have like $5, you should invest it in this stock because this is the pure-play AI leader,'" Shetty said. "I think of my father who invested in Microsoft during the dotcom bubble, and he divested from that stock, and it was such a silly thing to do."
Joe Pak, a former macro portfolio manager who is now an independent researcher outside London, is opting against participating in the Anthropic IPO for two reasons: the likelihood of limited allocation and current macroeconomic conditions.
He believes the odds are probably stacked against retail investors when it comes to the allocation of shares.
"It's very difficult as a retail investor to actually get an allocation in these blockbuster IPOs," the 36-year-old said. "You get maybe one share, and the base case is you don't get any at all. So, it's a bit of a catch-22. If you do get a lot of shares, it probably means that the institutional bid was weaker, and in that case, you don't actually want the shares at that level."
In terms of the economy, conditions "need to be favorable" to hold a position in a stock like Anthropic, he said. But with the Federal Reserve having raised interest rates in September and widely expected to do so again next month, the backdrop could be darkening.
"The risk that you have is the financial conditions deteriorating" before the company starts to grow into anticipated profit and revenue, which would justify purchase of the stock, Pak said.
While Pak is steering clear of the IPO, he did say that at a certain level, it would make sense to get into Anthropic.
Other retail investors such as Bryan Nearnberg share Pak's view.
"I'm planning to eventually buy Anthropic, just not at the IPO price, considering when the lockups expire and there's some selling pressure," said the 37-year-old Westchester County resident, who works in finance operations. "We are not at the end of this short-term negative headline sentiment."
IPOs are a sore spot for Nearnberg, who hasn't had much luck trading stocks on their opening day. His skepticism toward IPOs can be traced all the way back to when he was in college.
"I didn't get an allocation to the Facebook IPO, but I ended up buying it the first day of open. I got burned pretty quickly," Nearnberg told CNBC. "Same thing with Zynga. I didn't get an allocation, but [got] burned pretty quickly in terms of price."
As a result of those experiences, "I'm pretty sure we'll see a good entry price underneath the IPO for Anthropic by Memorial Day next year," Nearnberg said, citing sour sentiment toward technology and  concern surrounding circular financing as short-term headwinds.
To be clear, all the retail investors CNBC spoke with are optimistic on AI as a transformative technology — even the ones sitting out the IPO. One trader said he believes in AI so much that he uses Anthropic's Claude, a conversational AI assistant, every day.
But Russ Faigen, a 27-year-old in Austin, Texas, is undecided on whether to subscribe for a piece of the IPO.
"From a price-to-sales ratio, Anthropic's like a really good deal," Faigen said. But "it's still a massive valuation for a $1.4 trillion company, and there are significantly better deals out there if you are a fundamental investor."
Faigen, who works for an agentic brokerage firm, said he's "leaning towards patience," as he believes Anthropic is going to be public "for a very long time."
"I just am not in a rush to get in on day one based off the valuation," he told CNBC.
Anthropic's valuation depends on its ability to sustain its rapid growth. In the nine months through Sept. 30, revenue reached more than $33 billion, 1,200% above the year-earlier period. Aggregate spending commitments total about $900 billion , primarily centered around computing power and infrastructure.
Breakneck growth leads plenty of retail and institutional investors to approach not just the Anthropic IPO but the entire AI trade with caution.
"A lot of it comes down to scrutiny over how much money they're spending on AI," said Bret Kenwell, U.S. investment analyst at eToro. "Investors want to see that those investments are turning into tangible returns, into tangible revenue."

articles.title_orig: Apple Reportedly Developing Two Designs for 20th Anniversary iPhone
articles.title_zh: Apple Reportedly Developing Two Designs for 20th Anniversary iPhone
articles.content_orig:
Apple is currently developing four models with two different designs for the iPhone's 20th anniversary, according to the leaker known as "Ice Universe."
In a new post on Weibo , the leaker outlined the two designs. Two are said to feature flat glass covers and two have glass that curves along all four edges.
One plausible explanation for this is that Apple is developing two sizes (Pro and Pro Max models) with alternative designs, potentially retaining the flatter versions as fallbacks for the more ambitious curved design, rather than planning to launch four models. Another explanation is that the models with flat front glass are standard "iPhone 20" models set to launch after the iPhone 20 Pro.
The curved versions reportedly have bezels measuring around 1mm, but the shape of the surrounding glass makes them almost invisible when viewed head-on, creating an almost borderless appearance. Ice Universe suggested the effect would be particularly striking in person.
Apple has apparently been prototyping the four-sided curved glass design for three years, making several revisions during that time. The design choice is said to remain under consideration, with the earliest versions featuring substantially more pronounced curves that were later reduced.
The report is plausible since it echoes Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman 's report from August , which said that Apple had scrapped an earlier, more ambitious anniversary design that used even more glass in place of metal. Gurman said the design planned for 2027 still features curved front and rear glass separated by a thin metal band. Both reports suggest Apple has moderated elements of its original design.
The latest claims follow a series of design details about the rumored "iPhone 20 Pro" that have emerged in recent days. Screen protector samples circulating online show rounded edges with curves along all four sides and very narrow display borders. According to Ice Universe, the screen protectors seen in recent days reflects an early version with greater curvature.
Earlier this week, the leaker "Fixed Focus Digital" said the devices would use the same glass material as the iPhone Air , but with greater curvature along all four sides. An accompanying illustration depicted rounded front and rear glass meeting a narrow, polished metal frame.
Ice Universe added that industry sources are enthusiastic about the curved glass design, with some expressing greater anticipation for the anniversary model than for a foldable iPhone.
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027. While leakers have referred to the devices as the "iPhone 20 Pro," Apple's naming plans remain unclear.

articles.title_orig: 2028 Ford Mustang GTD Gets A Special Edition 125 Years In The Making
articles.title_zh: 2028 Ford Mustang GTD Gets A Special Edition 125 Years In The Making
articles.content_orig:
The Ford Mustang GTD is getting a few small tweaks for 2028. The automaker’s ultimate Pony Car gets a new special edition that celebrates "Sweepstakes"—the car Henry Ford built and raced in 1901 as a last-ditch effort to attract investors.
Ford won, and 125 years later, the Blue Oval is honoring that special car with a unique livery for the Mustang GTD. The new 1901 livery replaces last year's Spirit of America package and features Royal Red exterior paint with black accents. The splitter, diffuser, rockers, and rear wing feature exposed carbon fiber.
Inside, the 1901 livery comes with mahogany red leather seats and race red stitching. The Performance Package , which includes aerodynamic updates and a weight reduction, is standard.
2028 Ford Mustang GTD 1901
Beyond the new livery, the 2028 Mustang GTD gets redesigned 3D-printed titanium paddle shifters and a new shift ring. Full-grain leather now wraps around the center console, the door panels, and the instrument panel.
Optional magnesium wheels will also be available for the 2028 model year. Ford introduced them with the car's launch but has faced supplier constraints, which the automaker says have been resolved.
On the outside, Ford has new painted stripe options. There’s also an updated livery for the Liquid Carbon with teal accents and striping. Incognito Green and Teal Tonic exterior colors have been added, replacing Sage Green and Blue Metallic.
Ford didn’t touch the powertrain. Under the hood is Ford’s supercharged 5.2-liter V8 engine, with its dry-sump oil system. It still makes 815 horsepower and 664 pound-feet of torque, with a rear-mounted eight-speed dual-clutch transaxle.
The top speed remains 202 miles per hour, and Brembo ceramic brakes provide the stopping power for the Mustang . Ford will release pricing information closer to the Mustang’s on-sale date.
Interested buyers can begin placing orders in December, with deliveries expected to start in the second quarter of 2027.

articles.title_orig: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
articles.title_zh: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
articles.content_orig:
Waymo has temporarily stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways after California banned the vehicles from state freeways following recent traffic incidents.
The company had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.
A Waymo spokesperson wrote in an email that the company has “temporarily restricted commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service,” though it’s “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel.” The suspension was implemented last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they didn't say how long it would last.
Related video: Why are gas prices dropping and how low will they go?
The suspension came after the California Department of Motor Vehicles banned the company's robotaxis from freeways that same day. The ban followed two incidents including one in which three Waymo driverless vehicles drove into a construction zone, DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman said in a statement.
The construction zone incident occurred on Nov. 5 and the second incident, which involved California Highway Patrol vehicles, occurred the next day on a highway in San Francisco, according to Groveman.
Video of the Nov. 6 incident circulated widely on social media last week. In the footage, a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to bypass California Highway Patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break.
“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” Groveman said.
Groveman added that “similar incidents” previously occurred on May 18.
The Waymo spokesperson said the “recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California” did not “involve any injuries or collisions.”
California's restrictions bar Waymo from operating and testing its driverless vehicles on California freeways, according to Groveman. He said the restrictions will remain in effect until “Waymo demonstrates to the Department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.”
Kelety reported from Phoenix.

articles.title_orig: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
articles.title_zh: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
articles.content_orig:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday called for aggressive action against inflation , saying the central bank needs to "shock people" as prices continue to rise more than he expected.
In the near term, the policymaker told CNBC in a live interview that a half percentage point increase in the Fed's benchmark rate is probably necessary at the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
He said the central bank needs to reverse the three quarter-point reductions from last year and may need to do more.
"I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman during a " Squawk Box " interview. "If you really want to get it down, you've got to start taking more aggressive actions."
"You might need to, like, shock people," he said.
Futures prices are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the FOMC's December meeting. They also are anticipating another move in January, followed by at least one additional increase before the end of 2027, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge.
Waller said the Fed wouldn't necessarily have to approve a half-point hike in December if it raised rates by a quarter point and signaled another move coming in January. However, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has been against that kind of forward guidance on grounds that it ties policymakers' hands.
"If you're not going to signal this very clearly to markets, you're going in January, my view is then you have to go 50 [basis points] in December to put it in place and get it done," he said.
Recent statements from other central bankers indicate a range of opinions , though most agree that more policy tightening is needed to bring down inflation.
In a speech Tuesday, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested as many as four hikes by the spring of 2027. Some Fed officials, including regional Presidents Beth Hammack of Cleveland and Lorie Logan of Dallas, have endorsed more gradual tightening.
However, continued inflation above the Fed's 2% target might push officials into a more aggressive stance.
The FOMC approved its first interest rate hike in more than three years in September, and then held rates steady at its October meeting. While inflation has continued to run hot since then, other Fed officials seem less eager to drop the policy hammer as heavily as Waller.
"I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action," New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday in a conversation with Axios. "I think what we've been doing over the last past few months is ... working well. We're collecting the data, analyzing it, having the debate and making a decision."
The Fed in 2025 approved three rate cuts amid worries over the labor market and the belief that inflation would continue to moderate toward the central bank's 2% goal.
However, inflation reignited earlier this year after the strikes the U.S. and Israel launched against Iran in late February. Energy prices spiked while tariff impacts lingered, keeping most inflation readings above 3% .
"First of all, you've got to take back the three insurance cuts we put in last year," Waller said. "If the policy rate last summer in 2025 wasn't bringing inflation down, getting back to that isn't going to bring it down. So we may have to go above ... three hikes plus maybe some more to get it to start actually coming back down."
The FOMC later Wednesday will release minutes from the October meeting.
